transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Samantha Ortiz (PioneerHealth): Samantha here.
[00:08] Daniel Park: Daniel.
[00:09] Leah Kim: Leah.
[00:10] Tom Reyes: Tom.
[00:12] Jordan Lee: Great. Goal for today is to walk through SSO, SCIM provisioning and our RBAC model, answer any gaps for your security team. Priya will do a little demo, Marcus will cover audit/encryption stuff.
[00:25] Priya Raman (Redwood): Hi all - I'll start with the SAML flow. Essentially we support SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SAML. You'll need to share your Okta metadata, cert, and the assertion mapping you want for groups -> roles. A few customers call the audience the ACS URL, sometimes that trips people up.
[00:43] Leah Kim: We run Okta, yes. We do SCIM push today for other SaaS. Curious how Redwood handles group sync and group-to-role mapping, and importantly: how are users deprovisioned? We've seen stale accounts linger elsewhere.
[00:58] Priya Raman: Good question. Our SCIM implementation supports full create/update/delete (we handle POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE). Group sync can be configured to map a SCIM group to a Redwood role. On delete we honor the delete event and mark the user as deactivated immediately; we also support a configurable grace period before hard-delete if you prefer soft deprovisioning. Note: sometimes the word SCIM gets transcribed as "skim" in older exports, sorry if docs show that.
[01:21] Marcus Chu (Redwood): From security side, we also capture deprovision events into audit logs and emit the actor, timestamp, and reason (if provided by the IdP). Logs are stored in our audit pipeline and can be exported to your SIEM via syslog/s3/kinesis. Retention is configurable per contract - SOC 2 customers often do 12 months or longer.
[01:42] Daniel Park: For export, do you push to our S3 or we pull? We prefer push to a customer-owned S3 with SSE-KMS.
[01:48] Marcus Chu: We can push to your S3 using a cross-account role and write encrypted objects with SSE-KMS under your key. Alternatively, we can stream logs into your Splunk/Datadog via secure forwarders. Both patterns are used.
[02:05] Samantha Ortiz: On SAML: we need clarity around attributes - we want group claims to be present in the assertion so mapping is deterministic. Any limits on claim sizes?
[02:16] Priya Raman: We recommend sending group membership as a single repeating attribute (group claim), or using SCIM for large-scale membership. SAML assertions do have practical size limits on some IdPs and browsers - if you have >2k groups per assertion SCIM is safer.
[02:31] Tom Reyes: Do you support SCIM incremental PATCH semantics? Our workflows rely on PATCH for partial updates.
[02:36] Priya Raman: Yes, we support PATCH (RFC7644 semantics). In our implementation PATCH is idempotent for group membership changes; we also return 207 for multi-status where applicable. Some IdPs do PUT-only so we can accept either depending on your Okta config.
[02:51] Leah Kim: How do you map SCIM groups to roles? For example, we want a "clinician_readonly" and a "clinician_admin" mapped to different RBAC scopes.
[03:02] Jordan Lee: We give a role mapping table in the console where you can map SCIM group names to roles. Priya will show the mapping and policy editor. Roles are hierarchical and scope-limited; you can create custom roles too.
[03:15] Priya Raman: Demo: (screen share sounds) Here is the mapping UI — you can pick a group -> role mapping and choose whether it grants project-level access or org-level. Notice the least-privilege template; we ship templates for common personas like Reader, Operator, Admin.
[03:35] Samantha Ortiz: Are those templates audit-friendly? We need to show least-privilege during our internal SOC 2 prep.
[03:41] Marcus Chu: Yes - every role change, creation, and assignment is logged. We surface role assignment history per user in the audit UI and as part of the exported logs. For SOC 2 you can request the access control change logs for the period under review.
[03:56] Daniel Park: What about Just-in-Time provisioning or JIT? Sometimes we prefer SAML-based JIT for ephemeral guest accounts.
[04:03] Priya Raman: We support JIT provisioning via SAML assertion claims; when enabled, the assertion creates the user at first login and can map initial groups. However, for full lifecycle management and guaranteed deprovisioning, SCIM push is recommended.
[04:18] Leah Kim: Can we enforce MFA for Redwood console users coming from SSO? We want conditional access.
[04:23] Jordan Lee: Yes - Redwood respects the IdP's authentication context. If your Okta policy requires MFA, the SAML assertion will only reach us after MFA and we honor the assertion accordingly. We don't enforce an additional Redwood MFA if you rely on SSO. We also support SCIM-based role sync and session length controls per role.
[04:41] Samantha Ortiz: Encryption: Does Redwood use customer-managed keys for stored data and logs?
[04:46] Marcus Chu: For data at rest in Private deployments you can bring-your-own-KMS/HSM. For Redwood hosted we support BYOK for certain enterprise plans - i.e., we can encrypt at rest using your KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). Audit logs exported to your S3 can be encrypted with your KMS. For metadata that we store about user objects, those fields are encrypted at rest and access is logged.
[05:07] Daniel Park: If we rotate keys, how is re-encryption handled?
[05:10] Marcus Chu: Key rotation is handled by your KMS for envelope keys; for hosted BYOK we re-wrap envelope keys with the new CMK on rotation. For on-prem/private deployments you control the lifecycle. We'll include details in the KMS doc.
[05:22] Priya Raman: Back to SCIM attributes: typical attributes we consume: userName, name.familyName, name.givenName, emails[type eq "work"].value, active (true/false), externalId, and groups with displayName and members. We have an example attributes JSON we'll share.
[05:40] Leah Kim: For provisioning disabled accounts do you remove access immediately or keep sessions alive until expiry?
[05:46] Marcus Chu: We terminate new token issuance on deactivation immediately. Existing sessions are revoked on next token refresh; for long-lived sessions (if applicable) we support immediate session revocation for security-sensitive customers.
[06:00] Samantha Ortiz: Audit retention: can we keep immutable logs for 3 years?
[06:04] Marcus Chu: For enterprise plans we can arrange extended retention and WORM-style exports to your S3. That would be part of the contract.
[06:13] Tom Reyes: Are there any gotchas with SAML metadata - cert rollover or multiple certs?
[06:18] Priya Raman: We support multiple metadata entries and cert rotation. You can upload new metadata and we support a dual-cert window for rollover. We also support automatic certificate verification using the metadata URL.
[06:29] Daniel Park: If we want to test a SCIM sync, what's the recommended approach?
[06:33] Jordan Lee: Best practice: create a test Okta application pointed at our SCIM endpoint with a small test group (5-10 users). Send us the Okta tenant, a test service account, and we'll run a sync in a staging account. We'll coordinate with Leah on the test window.
[06:46] Leah Kim: Sounds good. Also, for role mapping I want a sample least-privilege policy for clinicians vs admin that restricts PHI export.
[06:55] Priya Raman: We have a policy template that toggles export rights and PII scopes. We'll attach that to the mapping template we send.
[07:04] Samantha Ortiz: One compliance ask: do you provide SOC 2 evidence reports or a SOC 2 letter?
[07:09] Marcus Chu: We can share our SOC 2 Type II attestation and the control mapping. For customer-specific evidence, we have a secure process that requires an NDA and access request. We'll send the standard SOC 2 pack now and a link to request additional artifacts.
[07:21] Jordan Lee: Quick recap before we close - action items and next steps: we'll send SAML metadata template, SCIM attribute examples, RBAC mapping template, and KMS details. Schedule the SCIM test for week of Feb 16. Any final questions?
[07:35] Tom Reyes: No, that's it. Thanks.
[07:37] Samantha Ortiz: Thank you.
[07:39] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by EOD with the docs.
[07:42] (call ends)

Notes: transcription occasionally mis-labels SCIM as "skim"; some timestamps are approximate. References: shared deck (link in chat), SCIM example JSON (to be sent), SOC 2 pack (secure link).
